chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Haytham ibn Abi Masrouq, from al-Hakam ibn Miskeen, from Muhammad ibn Marwan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
If two gutters were flowing, one of them being a gutter of urine and the other a gutter of water, and they mixed together, then it touches you, there would be no problem in it.

key_terms.بَأْس: Harm, problem, or legal impediment; 'lā ba's' (no problem) is a formulaic phrase indicating permissibility
key_terms.بَوْل: Urine; one of the major ritual impurities (najasah) in Islamic law
key_terms.مِيزَاب: Gutter, roof-spout, or drainage channel used to divert rainwater or waste water

ai.seo_question: Is water that has mixed with urine from a gutter ritually pure according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) issued a ruling on the ritual purity of water that has been mixed with urine from gutters flowing together. The ruling establishes that if water and urine from two separate gutters mix and then contact a person, it does not render them ritually impure. This reflects the Imami jurisprudential principle that large quantities of flowing water or sufficiently diluted impurities do not transfer ritual impurity.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Haysam Bin Abu Masrouq, from Al Hakam Bin Miskeen, from Muhammad Bin Marwan, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘If the two gutters are flowing, one of the two being of urine and the other one being of water, so they get mixed up, then it touches you, there would be no problem with it’.
en.sarwar: 2. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Haytham ibn abu Masruq from al-Hakam ibn Miskin from Muhammad ibn Marwan who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that
if two drain-shoots, one with rain water and the other with urine mix, and drops thereof sprinkle over one’s clothes, it is not harmful for him.”
